title: True Colours Boards Venice-Bound Female Sniper Drama ‘No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman’
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Marion Cotillard New Image & First Sales Unveiled For Nicole Garcia’s San Sebastian-Bound ‘Milo’ Italian Film Bodies Slam Venice Over Lack Of Women In Competition: “It’s A One-Dimensional, Male-Dominated Selection” Michael Pomeroy’s ‘Paul & Greg & Amelia’ With Quinn Jackson, Christopher Ryan, Matt Hardy & Terra Layne Wraps Ahead Of TIFF Sales Push View All July 28, 2026 4:14am No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman Hene Films EXCLUSIVE: Rome-based sales company True Colours has boarded Norwegian-Kurdish director Halkawt Mustafa’s drama No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman ahead of its world premiere Out of Competition at the Venice Film Festival in September. Avan Jamal stars as a female Peshmerga sniper who heads to Mosul to rescue her younger sister from ISIS, forcing her to confront the violence she survived and the shadows of the person she has become. The cast also features Thorbjørn Harr, Kanar Sarchl and Kader Jalal. Mustafa wrote, directed and produced the film, which is inspired by years of conversations with real Kurdish women who fought ISIS. Watch on Deadline The director previously explored the world of female Kurdish fighters with the 2015 documentary The Women ISIS Fears. “We are very happy to collaborate with True Colours on the film’s international journey. From our first conversations, the team understood both the film’s artistic vision and its universal message,” said Mustafa. The film is produced by Mustafa, Janne Hjeltnes and John M. Jacobsen for Hene Films, in co-production with The Chimney Pot (Sweden) and La Media (Iraq). “We are thrilled to be working on Halkawt’s film. An immensely engaging cinematic experience, it powerfully portrays the Kurdish people’s struggle through the eyes of a heroic female fighter,” said Fabio Tucci, Head of Acquisitions at True Colours. title: New Mike Leigh, Pablo Larrain Films in San Sebastian Competition
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 4:01am 'Tender Loving Care' © Joseph Lynn / ©️ Thin Man Films Ltd New films from Mike Leigh , Pablo Larrain and Hans Petter Moland are among the titles in the running for the Golden Shell at this year’s San Sebastian film festival . San Sebastian on Tuesday revealed additions to its 2026 competition selection, including Leigh’s British drama Tender Loving Care ; Moland’s Growth of the Soil ; and Larrain’s My Sad Dead — a Netflix mini-series that will be screened as single, 4-hour feature. Other competition highlights including Milo from director Nicole Garcia ( Oran ), a French drama featuring Marion Cotillard and Lurker star Théodore Pellerin ; and In My Father’s Room , the directorial debut of Japanese novelist Maha Harada. Related Stories Business How the World Cup Boosted Canal+ Results Movies Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven Two previous festival winners return, with Argentine director Benjamín Naishtat, winner of the Silver Shell for best director for Rojo in 2018, and the best screenplay honors for Puan in 2023, back in competition with Glaxo , a 1950s-set drama based on the novel of the same name by Argentine writer Hernán Ronsino and starring Lali Espósito, Marcelo Subiotto and Esteban Bigliardi. Turkish filmmaker Yeşim Ustaoğlu, whose Pandora’s Box (2008) won the Golden Shell, with lead Tsilla Chelton taking best actress, will present her latest, What Remains , at San Sebastian this year. San Sebastian previously announced three Spanish films in official competition: El mal padre from Roberto Bueso; 5 more minutes from Javier Ruiz Caldera; Saints from Mikel Gurrea. Out of competition, San Sebastian will screen two Spanish series: El castillo , created and written by Isabel Peña and Eduardo Villanueva and directed by Elena Martín Gimeno and Sandra Romero, and Beyond Society , from Carlos Torres. Special screenings include The Last Goodbye from Koldo Almandoz; Pray for Us from Daniel Monzón; The Harvester from David Pérez Sañudo; and Bajañí from Fernando Trueba. The 74th San Sebastián Festival runs from September 18-26. THR

title: Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’
full_text: Jul 28, 2026 3:24am PT Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ 36 minutes ago ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 51 minutes ago San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago See All MIFFest Xinemarte , the immersive cinematic art platform developed by Los Angeles-based creative technology company SQNXR, has made its Malaysia premiere as a special program at the recently concluded 9th Malaysia International Film Festival in Kuala Lumpur. The platform’s Kuala Lumpur rollout began a day ahead of MIFFest ‘s opening, and marks the second stop in Xinemarte’s Asian expansion following a soft launch in Taipei. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Says There Is 'Absolutely No Goddamn AI' in 'Pan's Labyrinth' 3D Re-Release: 'We're Protecting a Lineage of Art' 'Coyote vs. Acme' Director and Star Lana Condor on Finally Showing Their Film to the Fans at Comic-Con: 'The Fight Was For a Good Reason' The Malaysia program centers on “The Room Remembers,” Xinemarte’s inaugural thematic chapter, and its first presentation, “Fluid” – a 25-minute audiovisual work by SQNXR Creative Director Ray Tijssen, who operates under the alias 0010×0010. The work treats the movie theater itself as the primary artistic medium, drawing on cinematic-scale projection and Dolby Atmos surround sound to create a shared sensory environment. Popular on Variety “You have canvas, you have screens, you have sculpture and you have movie theatre rooms,” Tijssen said. “The room becomes the audience. The room remembers.” Tijssen described “Fluid” as “organic forms adrift in a single current, where solid and liquid move as one, somewhere between deep ocean and deep space.” MIFFest audiences attended a special post-screening Q&A session with Tijssen, in which he discussed the creative process behind the work and the concept underpinning “The Room Remembers.” The screenings drew a positive response from festival-goers, with many describing the experience as calming and meditative. Jazzy Group of Companies, the Malaysia-based entertainment company and MIFFest organizer, holds the exclusive Asia sales mandate for Xinemarte. CEO Joanne Goh founded the festival. “Cinema infrastructure is underutilized for significant portions of the day,” Goh said. “Xinemarte allows operators to activate those spaces with premium experiential content that appeals to audiences who might never attend a traditional film screening. We see enormous potential across the region.” Structured around 25-minute cycles with staggered start times, the platform allows audiences to enter and exit freely, with programming updated monthly across family-friendly and adult-oriented categories. Rather than adapting conventional content for cinema screens, Xinemarte was built to exploit the full capabilities of contemporary theatrical infrastructure. Following its Malaysia run, the platform is set to expand to Singapore, Hong Kong and additional markets across the region. Tijssen, who was born in the Netherlands and is now based in Los Angeles, has previously mounted installations at MOCA Bangkok, W1 London and TODA Dubai. title: Revealed: The Early-Stage Plans For A New TV Festival In Edinburgh
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Cristiano Ronaldo Reportedly Lining Up First Drama Series With Matthew Vaughn, Damian Lewis & Some Big Name Guest Stars Chris Brown Pleads Guilty To Affray Over UK Nightclub Confrontation View All July 28, 2026 3:15am Richard Gadd; Edinburgh Fringe and Phoebe Waller-Bridge Josh Telles for Deadline/Getty EXCLUSIVE: With the TV Festival leaving Edinburgh for the first time in its 51-year history, organizers in the Scottish capital are refusing to rest on their laurels. Deadline can reveal that early-stage plans are afoot to launch a new TV festival in Edinburgh. These plans have been hatched prior to the final one taking place in less than a month’s time and are understood to have been discussed at a recent roundtable with figures from the local sector. Screen Scotland , the body that represents the interests of the Scottish film and TV industry, commissioned a piece of work earlier this year examining what a new fest might look like along with the implications of the TV Festival’s relocation for the Scottish screen sector and wider Edinburgh festivals landscape. The expectation from many was that Edinburgh would lose its role as host city to Greater Manchester , home of new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham , and organizers in Edinburgh wanted to get ahead of the game. Related Stories Festivals Christine Vachon, Ewan McGregor & Sarah Brocklehurst Among Names Set For Edinburgh Film Festival's 2026 Industry Programme News Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film 'These Violent Delights' -- First Look Trailer Rowan Woods, the former creative chief at the Edinburgh TV Festival , has been leading on this work for months as an independent consultant. Woods, whose role was limited to the research and report itself, has just reported back to Screen Scotland with a set of recommendations and range of options. Watch on Deadline While we have not seen the recommendations, Deadline is told that Woods delivered a number of them and they are varied. They were discussed at a roundtable last week in Glasgow with around 20 figures from the local TV industry, we understand. The decision whether to push on with a new festival now lies with Screen Scotland. We hear an announcement could be made in the coming weeks, possibly before the final TV Festival starts on August 25. A Screen Scotland spokeswoman told Deadline the body has been “working with partners since the spring to explore options should the TV Festival’s board decide – as it now has – to break with the event’s history and move the festival to England.” The spokeswoman added that Screen Scotland is “looking at the opportunity for innovation in August provided by the TV Festival’s departure and exploring the best way to continue to support Scotland-based production businesses to access key TV decision makers in Edinburgh during August.” Were this new Edinburgh fest to run in August, which given the timing of the world-famous Edinburgh Fringe would make perfect sense, it would be parking its tanks almost directly on the lawn of the TV Festival in Greater Manchester , which will also likely take place in August. The relocation of the TV Festival has been a huge story for the industry this year and connected sources said there is now a political will in Scotland to get behind another event. Scottish government officials were clear to TV Festival executives and its board members during the bidding process that they would back a new event if Edinburgh lost the fest, we understand. Our story also comes as the Edinburgh International Film Festival expands. Deadline revealed last month that the fest is launching a conference , with first speaker set as BFI chief Ben Roberts, while the majority of last year’s competition titles landed distribution in the UK and U.S. “The world comes here in August” Hollywood royalty Shonda Rhimes was awarded , ast year’s inaugural Edinburgh Fellowship. Image: Edinburgh TV Festival Unsurprisingly, in what is an incredibly connected Scottish TV industry, there have been rumblings and mutterings about the potential for a new festival for weeks. Deadline spoke to a number of executives, all of whom had heard these rumors but were split on the shape they thought a new fest should take, or whether Edinburgh should host one at all. One indie boss, who has been heavily involved with the fest over the years, said the Edinburgh Fringe in August allows the city to offer something “different and unique.” Organizers of any new fest must therefore think big, think global and be talent-led, this source said, providing something that contrasts with other UK industry events that have become a crucial part of the annual TV calendar like Content London, the London TV Screenings and the Creative Cities Convention, along with, of course, the new TV Festival in Greater Manchester. “The world comes here in August,” said the indie boss. “American agencies, book publishers, high-profile talent and decision makers arrive in Edinburgh and want to be there. If there’s a date in your calendar that allows you to have fun and maybe find the next [ Baby Reindeer creator Richard] Gadd, well which would you choose?” This indie boss put forward the argument made by many prior to the fest relocation decision being made, which was that relocating the fest would sever talent pipelines by ending the TV Festival’s alchemy with the Fringe. Speaking to Deadline back in March, a frustrated Jon Thoday, who runs agency-producer Avalon, said “no-one from Avalon [will be going to the TV Festival in Greater Manchester] if I’ve got anything to do with it.” His argument goes that TV commissioners and executives discover the talent of tomorrow like Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Gadd and many more via the Fringe when they come to the TV Festival. On the other side of the coin, one Scottish industry executive said a new fest gifts an opportunity to think locally. “I think the money would be better spent on helping freelancers or production companies with training,” he added. “We could do a freelancers festival that is more sustainable and affordable.” This person questioned whether those in charge of the new fest will opt for a “glamor project” over their more local proposal. However, a different indie boss based out of Scotland pondered whether a local fest would feel “small, parochial and poorly attended” when compared with the might of the relocated TV Festival. In difficult times and with commissioning opportunities dimming, this source queried whether there needs to be a festival at all. “It’s too late,” they mused. “If there is any spare money honestly I would spend it on grants to enable good quality program ideas to happen. We need to create jobs for freelancers and production companies.” Regardless of its potential to be seen as a break from the past, any new fest would have big shoes to fill. The Edinburgh TV Festival has spent 50 years attracting thousands of the great and the good of the industry along with plenty from the other side of the pond including, just last year, Hollywood royalty in Shonda Rhimes and Tina Fey. Its annual MacTaggart lecture is often a headline grabber and it always features talks from the top network heads including the new BBC Director General this year for what will be his first big set-piece address. In what is a crowded UK events calendar, the Edinburgh – soon to be Greater Manchester – TV Festival clearly remains one of the year’s focal points. Industry eyes are trained on what happens next. Work has already begun. title: ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE)

The film will open locally as “Mãi Nợ Một Lời Tạm Biệt,” rendered in English as “The Farewell I Never Gave.” The international title remains “Chrysalis.” The deal marks a significant distribution milestone for the U.S.-Vietnam production, which is set in Vietnam and draws on the childhood memories of its subject and executive producer, Sir Daniel K. Winn. “Bringing ‘Chrysalis’ to theaters in Vietnam is deeply personal,” Winn said. “This story grew out of my childhood and the love of my grandmother, and I hope Vietnamese audiences see something of their own families and memories in it.” Related Stories 'Haunting Adeline' Adult Graphic Novels in the Works Based on H.D. At DANAFF, Kieu Chinh received the Screen Excellence Merit Award, recognizing a screen career spanning nearly seven decades and more than 100 roles. “‘Chrysalis’ is a deeply moving story that explores the powerful themes of family and memory,” CJ CGV Vietnam said in a statement. “We look forward to bringing this remarkable award-winning film to audiences across Vietnam this September.” The Vietnam theatrical run is part of the film’s broader release schedule, which includes a Beverly Hills engagement in October and a worldwide rollout planned for November. title: Marion Cotillard New Image & First Sales Unveiled For Nicole Garcia’s San Sebastian-Bound ‘Milo’
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Canal+ Pledges More Than $1 Billion For French & European Cinema Over Five Years Italian Film Bodies Slam Venice Over Lack Of Women In Competition: “It’s A One-Dimensional, Male-Dominated Selection” Michael Pomeroy’s ‘Paul & Greg & Amelia’ With Quinn Jackson, Christopher Ryan, Matt Hardy & Terra Layne Wraps Ahead Of TIFF Sales Push View All July 28, 2026 2:50am Milo ©️ 2026 TRÉSOR FILMS - STUDIOCANAL - FRANCE 3 CINÉMA - MARCEL FILMS - LES FILMS PELLEAS - ARTEMIS PRODUCTIONS EXCLUSIVE: Studiocanal and Trésor Films have unveiled a new image of Marion Cotillard and Théodore Pellerin in Nicola Garcia’s Milo to coincide with the film being announced for competition in San Sebastian Film Festival’s 74th edition in September. Studiocanal, which co-produces and is handling international sales, has also posted a handful of early deals on the work with the film acquired for Canada (Mongrel Media), Scandinavia (Scanbox), Switzerland (Frenetic), Greece (Spenzos), Portugal (Lusomundo), CIS (Capella) and Ex-Yugoslavia (MCF). Studiocanal will handle the release in Germany. Related Stories News Mike Leigh's 'Tender Loving Care' & Pablo Larraín Series 'My Sad Dead' Among Titles Added To San Sebastian Lineup News Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa's MultiChoice Billed as a tale of “buried wounds, impossible choices and the fragile hope of rebuilding the bonds that define us”, Milo stars Cotillard as a woman called Alice who arrives in a quiet provincial town and takes a job at a local café, blending easily into a life that isn’t hers. Watch on Deadline It soon becomes apparent that her presence is no coincidence. She is there because of Milo (Pellerin), a young mechanic who works at a nearby garage. To him, Alice is a stranger. To her, he is someone tied to a past she has never truly left behind. It has been a high profile year on the festival circuit for Vie en Rose Oscar winner Cotillard who was at Cannes in May in Guillaume Canet’s Karma and Bertrand Mandico’s Roma Elastica, as she steps up the pace on her acting commitments. She previously worked with Garcia on her penultimate film, the post-WW2 romantic drama From the Land of the Moon . “The new role is diametrically opposed to the role of From the Land of the Moon . There was an emotional romanticism in that film, while here, on the contrary, it’s a much quieter role, contained, and deeply felt,” Garcia told Deadline of Cotillard’s role back in February . “There’s a silence filled with emotions and confessions that are difficult to express. You can sense her character has grown accustomed to the silence but is also grappling with it. It’s a real balancing act and it takes a great actress to pull that off.” Co-star Pellerin has made waves over the past year for for his performance as a young man diagnosed with throat cancer in Pauline Loquès’ 2025 Cannes Critics Week title Nino, for he won the Best Male Hope Cesar in February as well as the Louis Roederer Foundation Rising Star Award. Further cast members include Artus ( A Little Something Extra ), Alexis Manenti ( Undercover ), Anne Brochet ( Cyrano de Bergerac ), Éric Elmosnino ( The Belier Family ) and Charles Berling ( What’s In A Name ). Garcia directs from a screenplay she co-wrote with longtime collaborator Jacques Fieschi, with the collaboration of Laurette Polmanss and Olivier Demangel. The film marks the fourth collaboration between producer and Trésor Films head Alain Attal and Garcia, after Charlie Says , A View of Love and From The Land of the Moon . The film is co-produced by Canal+ subsidiary Studiocanal – which holds worldwide distribution rights and handles worldwide sales – with France 3 Cinéma, Marcel Films and Artémis Productions, with the support of CANAL+, Ciné+ OCS and France Télévisions. The picture will be released in French cinemas on January 20, 2027. title: San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More
full_text: Jul 28, 2026 2:31am PT San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More Nicole Garcia’s ‘7:40 ce matin-là/Milo,’ ‘In My Father’s Room,’ from Maha Harada, Hans Petter Moland’s ‘Growth of the Soil’ and Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s ‘What Remains’ also make San Sebastián’s main competition cut By John Hopewell , Emiliano De Pablos 'My Sad Dead' Credit: Pablo Larraín / Netflix Buzzy new projects from “Jacky,” “Spencer” and “Maria” director Pablo Larraín , and Benjamín Naishtat will be joined by Mike Leigh ’s “Tender Loving Care” in main competition at September’s San Sebastián Film Festival . Also making the cut are new titles from Nicole Garcia – Marion Coillard starrer “7:40 ce matin-là/Milo,’ as well as Maha Harada’s “In My Father’s Room,” Hans Petter Moland’s “Growth of the Soil” and Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s “What Remains.” Announced Tuesday, the new titles reflect San Sebastián’s hallmark mix of international name auteurs – often drawn from its key source markets of Latin America, France and the Nordics – and newer talent, a key focus for San Sebastián whose New Directors strand, set to be announced on Friday, is one of the most prestigious in Europe. Related Stories 'Star Trek' Sets 60th Anniversary & 'Strange New Worlds' Comic-Con Hall H Panels, Fan Screening, Activations (EXCLUSIVE) 'Futurama' to Release Three New Supersized Specials, Including a Christmas Episode, Starting Next Year on Hulu A feature version of Larraín’s Netflix four-part horror miniseries produced by Fabula, “My Sad Dead” (“Mis muertos tristes”) adapts Argentinean writer Mariana Enriquez, who suggests that the true terror is not the supernatural itself, but the horrors that society hides. Top Argentine actors Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi and Alejandra Flechner star. Popular on Variety Leigh’s “Tender Loving Care” stars Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson in what the festival describes as his “insightful exploration of the modern world.” From the director of “Rojo,” a big hit at San Sebastián, Naishtat’s “Glaxo” is a tale of shattered friendship set in a small provincial town between the late 1950s and the 1980s and described as “about desire and revenge, set at a time when a whole country lost its innocence.” San Sebastián’s newly announced Golden Shell contenders join three Spanish features in main competition which were announced on July 17: Mikel Gurrea’s “Sants,” with “The Beloved” star Vicky Luengo, top comedian Berto Romero’s time-loop relationship comedy “Five Minutes More” and Roberto Bueso’s family dramedy “El mal padre.” The 74th edition of the San Sebastian Film Festival, the biggest film event in the Spanish-speaking world, runs Sept. 18-26 in the capital of Gipuzcoa, in Spain’s verdant and stunning Basque Country. Newly Announced San Sebastián Main Competition Titles “Glaxo” (Benjamín Naishtat, Brazil/Argentina) Cast: Lali Espósito, Esteban Lamothe, and Marcelo Subiotto Produced by Brazil’s RT Features and Argentina’s Rei Pictures with a top Argentine cast of Espósito (“Permitidos,” “Sky Rojo”), Esteban Lamothe (“The Student”) and Marcelo Subiotto (“Puan”) and a tale which explores macro historical transformation via an intimate narrative, a winning combination in Rojo’s pre-junta portrayal of “moral apocalypse,” as Variety noted. “Growth of the Soil” (“Markens Grode,” Hans Petter Moland, Norway-Denmark-Germany) Cast: Herbert Nordrum, Asta Kamma August, Gard B. Eidsvold A stranger crossing the mountains of northern Norway anchors Moland’s adaptation of Knut Hamsun’s 1917 Nobel Prize-winning novel. Rootless Isak settles on barren land and attempts to build a life with Inger, a solitary woman marked by resilience and secrecy. Together they endure the elements, cultivate the soil and raise a family, only for time, hardship and desire to reshape them. Moland’s “Zero Kelvin” won San Sebastián’s Special Jury Prize in 1995. “In My Father’s Room” (“Muyou no hito,” Maha Harada, Japan) Cast: Aoi Yu, Ogata Issey, Nagayama Eita, Watanabe Eri Best-selling novelist Harada makes her director’s feature debut with an adaptation of her novel “An Unnecessary Man.” The film follows an art museum employee led by a mysterious key to a room once used by her recently deceased father. Retracing his final days, she discovers a life sustained by language, tea ceremony and overlooked beauty. Bitters End handles international sales and will release the drama in Japan in January 2027. ‘Milo’ Courtesy: San Sebastian Film Festival “Milo” (“7:40 ce matin-là,” Nicole Garcia, France) Cast: Marion Cotillard, Théodore Pellerin, Artus, Laure Calamy Garcia reunites with Oscar winner Cotillard after “From the Land of the Moon” for the story of a woman newly released from prison who takes a café job in a provincial town to approach Milo, a young mechanic unaware of their shared past. As buried tensions surface, both face the possibility of rebuilding a bond shattered decades earlier. From Garcia, a three-time Cannes competition contender (“From the Land of the Moon,” Selon Charlie,” “The Adversary”) And 14-time Cesar Award nominee. “My Sad Dead,” (“Mis muertos tristes,” Pablo Larraín, Argentina-Chile) Cast: Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Carolina Álvarez A world premiere. Ema, who can see and hear the dead, receives an unexpected visit from her niece Julie, who shares the same unsettling gift. As family secrets and wounds, resurface the entire neighborhood senses presences and hear the distinctive sounds of their own dead. Written by Larráin and among co-scribes, Guillermo Calderón, co-writer of “Neriuda” “El Conde,” and adapting Mariana Enríquez. “Mariana’s writing is particularly visual, always brilliant, and always dangerous. It’s a casual, domestic horror that inspires,” says Larraín. “What Remains” (“Artakalan,” Yeşim Ustaoğlu, Turkey-France-Luxembourg-Bulgaria) Cast: Öykü Karayel, Metin Akdülger, Ali Kayra Kul, İlyas Salman The portrait of a poet’s attempt to reclaim her inner voice. Breaking free from a suffocating domestic order, she reconnects with her conscience and begins questioning accepted ideas of family and the meaning of life. Her choices also open a different path for those around her. Ustaoğlu returns to San Sebastián, where “Pandora’s Box” won the Golden Shell in 2008 and Tsilla Chelton shared the acting prize. ‘Tender Loving Care’ Courtesy: San Sebastian Film Festival “Tender Loving Care,” (Mike Leigh, U.K./U.S./Singapore) Cast: Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, and Alice Bailey Johnson. title: Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ & Pablo Larraín Series ‘My Sad Dead’ Among Titles Added To San Sebastian Lineup
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Animaginary Partners With Gersh To Rep Worldwide Rights On Michael Mankowski’s ‘Getting Lost’ Animated Series Armand Assante To Narrate Documentary Feature ‘The Streets of Little Italy: 100 Years Of San Gennaro’ Christine Vachon, Ewan McGregor & Sarah Brocklehurst Among Names Set For Edinburgh Film Festival’s 2026 Industry Programme View All July 28, 2026 2:29am Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care' © Joseph Lynn / Thin Man Films Ltd. Mike Leigh’s latest feature Tender Loving Care and My Sad Dead , a new series from Chilean filmmaker Pablo Larraín, are among the titles that were announced this morning for the San Sebastian Film Festival. Scroll down for the full list of titles. My Sad Dead will screen at San Sebastian in its feature-length format. Starring are Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, and Carolina Álvarez. The project is based on four short stories by Mariana Enríquez, and tells the story of Ema, a woman with the ability to see and hear the dead. The San Sebastian screening will be a World Premiere. Related Stories Festivals San Sebastián Film Festival Appoints New Director News 'Los Domingos' Claims Golden Shell, 'The Voice Of Hind Rajab' Takes Audience Award At San Sebastián Film Festival - Full List Of Winners Leigh’s Tender Loving Care will arrive at San Sebastian after a world premiere at TIFF. Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, and Alice Bailey Johnson star in the film. No synopsis for Tender Loving Care has been provided on either the San Sebastian or TIFF website. San Sebastian simply describes the film as an “insightful exploration of the contemporary world.” Watch on Deadline Other titles added to San Sebastian today include 7:40 ce matin-là / Milo , the latest feature film from Nicole Garcia. Marion Cotillard and Théodore Pellerin star in the project, which tells the story of a woman fresh out of jail as she takes on a waitress job in a café to get closer to a young boy who works in the area. Norwegian filmmaker Hans Petter Moland also returns to the San Sebastian Official Selection with Markens Grode / Growth of the Soil , a story set in northern Norway about a couple who must put their love to the test when faced with looming challenges. The film is based on the Nobel Prize-winning novel by Knut Hamsun. Today’s titles join the nine films already announced for the Official Selection. Those titles include El mal padre , from Roberto Bueso; Sants / Saints , from Mikel Gurrea; and 5 minutos más / 5 more minutes , from Javier Ruiz Caldera. The 2026 San Sebastian Film Festival runs from September 18 to 26. San Sebastian 2026: 7:40 ce matin-là / MILO Nicole Garcia (Algeria) Country(ies) of production: France. Cast: Marion Cotillard, Théodore Pellerin, Artus , Laure Calamy, Alexis Manenti, Anne Brochet, Eric Elmosnino, Charles Berling Alice arrives in a quiet provincial town and takes a job at a local café, blending easily into a life that isn’t hers. Her presence is no coincidence. She is there because of Milo, a young mechanic who works at a nearby garage. To him, Alice is a stranger. To her, he is someone tied to a past she has never truly left behind. As buried tensions begin to surface and Milo drifts toward uncertain ground, both are pushed to a crossroads: is it possible to rebuild a bond that shattered decades ago? Artakalan / What Remains Yeşim Ustaoğlu (Turkey) Country(ies) of production: Turkey – France – Luxembourg – Bulgaria. Cast: Öykü Karayel, Metin Akdülger, Ali Kayra Kul, İlyas Salman A poetess breaks out of her suffocating life in order to get back in touch with her inner voice and conscience, questioning accustomed concepts of family and the meaning of life and paving a new path for her family members, as well. Glaxo Benjamín Naishtat (Argentina) Country(ies) of production: Brazil – Argentina. Cast : Lali Espósito, Marcelo Subiotto, Esteban Bigliardi, Esteban Lamothe, Manu Fanego, Alan Sabbagh Chivilcoy, 1957. In a quiet Argentinian town, the arrival of an ominous former police commissioner and his seductive wife fractures the bond between four inseparable young men. Decades later, the past resurfaces, forcing them to confront old wounds, guilt, and the possibility of revenge in a country which has lost its innocence. Markens Grode / Growth of the Soil Hans Petter Moland (Norway) Country(ies) of production: Norway – Denmark – Germany. Cast: Herbert Nordrum, Asta Kamma August, Gard B. Eidsvold A stranger appears over the mountain, carrying little more than his determination. Isak, a man without a past, seeks a place to settle and carve life from the earth. High above the tree line, he finds a barren stretch of land, as unforgiving as it is full of promise. The land tests him to his limits, until he meets Inger, a solitary woman shaped by resilience and quiet secrecy. Together, they endure the elements and build a life, cultivating both the soil and a growing family as the seasons turn. Yet as years pass and the world closes in, and time, hardship, and desire reshape them. Mis muertos tristes / My Sad Dead Pablo Larraín (Chile) Country(ies) of production: Argentina – Chile. Cast: Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Carolina Álvarez Based on the work from Mariana Enriquez and directed by Pablo Larraín, My Sad Dead follows Ema, who can see and hear the dead. After her mother’s death, Ema receives an unexpected visit from her niece Julie, with whom she shares the same unsettling gift. With Julie’s return, family secrets and wounds that never fully healed will resurface —but so will a strange phenomenon from which no one will emerge unscathed. The entire neighborhood will sense presences and hear the distinctive sounds of their own dead. Muyou no hito / In My Father’s Room Maha Harada (Japan) Country(ies) of production: Japan. Cast: Yu Aoi, Issey Ogata, Eita Nagayama, Eri Watanabe Satomi works at an art museum until an envelope arrives, containing a mysterious key. It leads to an unknown room once belonging to her late father, who died alone a month earlier. Drawn by this small object, she retraces his final days: a man seemingly left behind by society, yet sustained by a quiet devotion to words, the art of tea, and subtle beauty. Through the traces of his solitude, Satomi slowly discovers the quiet grace of the world he inhabited. Tender Loving Care Mike Leigh (United Kingdom) Country(ies) of production: United Kingdom – USA – Singapore. Cast: Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson Cannes Festival’s Palme d’Or winner and Academy Award nominee Mike Leigh returns with his next feature film, continuing his insightful exploration of the contemporary world. title: CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’
full_text: Jul 28, 2026 2:26am PT CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’ 2 hours ago Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’ 23 hours ago Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 1 day ago See All Screenshot courtesy The Daily Show on YouTube/Getty Images CNN ‘s Kaitlan Collins was “not surprised” that U.S. President Donald Trump insulted her during his speech at Friday night’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner. During an appearance on “The Daily Show” on Monday, Collins — who serves as CNN’s chief White House correspondent — debriefed the event with Jon Stewart. “In the room, I was not surprised when he insulted me. That happens pretty regularly inside the Oval Office. This is just a bigger venue where it was happening,” Collins said. “What was most surprising to me was — the room was filled with a lot of his staffers, his cabinet, his allies, Republicans in Congress — it was so quiet in the room during the president’s remarks.” Related Stories Ryan Reynolds Snuck Into Comic-Con as Deadpool With 'No Handlers' and 'No Security': 'I Felt So Lucky' Neon Bringing Na Hong-Jin’s 'Hope' to Comic-Con (EXCLUSIVE) “Do you think it’s because of how much they respect him?” Stewart asked, to which Collins cheekily replied: “Who’s to say.” Popular on Variety Collins received an award for her coverage of Trump’s contentious meeting with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky during the dinner, which was rescheduled from April after a gunman crashed through security at the original event. In his speech, the president said Collins “shouldn’t get the award” and that it was “fake,” and then went on a tangent about how she should smile more. Trump also compared Collins to trans advocate Dylan Mulvaney, mentioning the 2023 Bud Light controversy where conservative customers boycotted the beer brand after Mulvaney posted a social media ad featuring her face on a can. “I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said in his speech. Mulvaney responded to Trump in a TikTok video on Sunday, saying she was “honored” to be compared to Collins and the president’s attack was perhaps the “greatest compliment of all.” As Collins said, Trump has a history of insulting her and deflecting her questions, which Stewart pointed out are often pretty straightforward. “That’s why I ask the questions the way I do, is because I want anyone to be able to listen to what I’m asking — whether that’s at a briefing or during a moment with the president — and think, you know, I want to know the answer to that, too, or that is a good question,” Collins said. “I don’t want it to only serve one audience or one political leaning, I want anyone — from my family in Alabama, to people in the White House, to people in Washington — to be able to hear that question and think, ‘What is the answer to that?'” Collins also thanked her CNN colleague Wolf Blitzer, who presented the awards to journalists at the dinner, saying that “he’s called me every day since Friday.” She concluded that despite Trump’s speech, “It’s really not about me and I don’t want it to be about my reaction.” “I think if you let it become about that, then it becomes a back-and-forth between the two of us,” she said. “And instead, I think it’s more effective to remind people in those moments where he is insulting me or he is criticizing me, about the question I asked or the reporting I did that he was so angry about in this moment — and the fact that I got an award for it really bothered him, clearly.” Watch Collins’ full interview on “The Daily Show” below. title: How the World Cup Boosted Canal+ Results
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 28, 2026 2:02am Teboho Mokoena #4 of South Africa is challenged by Tomas Soucek #22 of Czechia during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group A match between Czechia and South Africa at Atlanta Stadium on June 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Lars Baron/Getty Images The $2 billion acquisition of Africa’s MultiChoice Group boosted Canal+ Group’s first-half financials, with the 2026 FIFA World Cup contributing to strong subscriber growth at the pay-TV giant’s South African business. “Following the acquisition of MultiChoice, our increased scale is starting to deliver the benefits we expected,” Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada said on Tuesday in unveiling the results. “We have achieved half of our €250 million ($284 million) synergies target and remain well on track for the year, and we confirm our full-year and medium-term guidance.” Related Stories Movies Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven Movies Netflix Sets Launch Date for Lee Chang-dong's Awards Hopeful 'Possible Love' Canal+ touted that “subscriber acquisition [was] up 40 percent, compared to the first half of 2025 in MultiChoice countries,” adding that June was the “best subscriber acquisition month in South Africa in a decade.” In that context, the company also mentioned “successful content and marketing initiatives, including the World Cup advertising campaign featuring Idris Elba and the launch of the Novelas+ channel in South Africa.” BNP Paribas analyst Nicolas Langlet was optimistic about the momentum at MultiChoice, writing in a report: “Trend at MultiChoice improved sequentially … driven by the success of FIFA World Cup and the first effects of the key initiatives implemented as part of the plan to boost growth. Thanks to the new strategy and reinvestment plan, we expect the subscriber base to improve in the second part of the year and support positive organic sales momentum exiting 2026.” Meanwhile, at production unit StudioCanal, Saada lauded “excellent six months on and off screen,” mentioning such box-office hits as Guru in France and Pressure in the U.S. “With a slate including Paddington 4 , Zack Snyder’s remake of Escape From New York , our first major South African film production, The Road Home , and Danny Boyle’s Ink , StudioCanal’s momentum looks set to continue,” he said. Canal+’s “content production, distribution and other” segment, which includes StudioCanal and streaming service Dailymotion, saw first-half revenue jump 9.9 percent, but adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) dropped 3 percent. Total Canal+ group revenue jumped 40 percent to €4.29 billion ($4.88 billion), driven by the MultiChoice takeover. Adjusting for the deal, growth came in at 1.4 percent. Adjusted EBIT jumped by 68 percent or, when excluding MultiChoice, rose 13 percent. THR

title: Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow
full_text: Jul 28, 2026 1:31am PT Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘The Odyssey’ Holds Top Spot as Vijay’s ‘Jana Nayagan’ Bows at No. 5 at U.K. and Ireland Box Office 18 minutes ago Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ 57 minutes ago ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago See All Netflix Lee Chang-dong ‘s “ Possible Love ” will open in Korean theaters September 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia Oct. 22 and in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland and Japan Oct. 23, before streaming globally on Netflix starting November 6. The film’s world premiere will be at the Venice Film Festival and North American Premiere at the Toronto Film Festival. “Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages. Related Stories 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' TV Series Casts Audiobook Star Jeff Hays as Princess Donut's Voice Ryan Reynolds Snuck Into Comic-Con as Deadpool With 'No Handlers' and 'No Security': 'I Felt So Lucky' The cast brings together Jeon Do-yeon (“Secret Sunshine”), Sul Kyung-gu (“Peppermint Candy”), Zo In-sung (“Escape From Mogadishu”) and Cho Yeo-jeong (“Parasite”) in what stands as one of the largest gatherings of top-tier Korean acting talent in a single film. Popular on Variety Lee also co-wrote the screenplay with Oh Jung-mi. Discovery for HBO Max (EXCLUSIVE) A 'gonzo' revenge thriller, 'Kill Jackie' has been picked up for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France and Belgium where the series will debut in 2026 By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More 1 hour ago ‘Kill Jackie,’ Starring a Glamorous, Lethal Catherine Zeta-Jones, Acquired by Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired revenge thriller “ Kill Jackie ,” starring Catherine Zeta-Jones , for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France and Belgium. The deal takes in two of HBO’s most established streaming markets, the Nordics and Spain, where SVOD services HBO Nordics and HBO España launched as far back as 2012 and 2016 with HBO Max set to pass Prime Video to become the second largest streamer in Spain by the end of 2026, according to Ampere Analysis. Related Stories 'Family Guy' Casts Kieran Culkin to Play the Devil in New Halloween Special for Hulu 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' TV Series Casts Audiobook Star Jeff Hays as Princess Donut's Voice Produced by Fremantle , which handles all international distribution outside the U.S., and Steel Spring Pictures, the eight-part series is scheduled to debut in 2026. “Kill Jackie” looks set to give Zeta-Jones, an Oscar, Bafta and Tony Award winner (“Chicago,” “Wednesday”), as she has recognised, a “multifaceted” role encompassing “empowerment, identity and redemption.” Popular on Variety Zeta-Jones plays a drug dealer turned glamorous art dealer whose past suddenly caches up with her as she becomes the target of The Seven Demons, a hit squad of the world’s most terrifying assassins. When a tragic event makes her hell-bent for revenge, Jackie determines to take out the Demons one by one, unleashing her old killer instincts. “However, she soon realises her own demons are much more terrifying than the ruthless killers on her trail…and her buried secrets ultimately lead her much closer to home, with surprising consequences,” the synopsis runs. A buzz title at the London TV Screenings, “Kill Jackie” co-stars Daniel Ings (“The Knight of the Seven Kingdoms”) as Jackie’s foil, her distinctly sensitive-about-violence tax lawyer, who, according to reports, provides much of the humor in a consistently high-octane, twisting, comedic thriller. Written by Tom Butterworth (“Gangs of London”) and Conor Keane, “Kill Jackie” is lead directed by Damon Thomas (“Killing Eve”), adapting “The Price You Pay” by Sunday Times best-selling author Nick Harkaway, writing as Aidan Truhen. Key cast also takes in another HBO alum, Sidse Babett Knudsen (“Prime Target,” “Borgen”),and Óscar Jaenada , Hattie Hook, Darci Shaw, Raff Law , Enzo Cilenti, Christine Adams, Julian Rhind-Tutt, Karlis Arnolds Avots, Set Sjöstrand, Tadashi Ito, Sebastian Armesto, Julian Barratt, Gavin Spokes , Jonathan Cake, Bamshad Abedi-Amin and Bill Paterson. “HBO Max has an outstanding track record of partnering on the very best projects, making it the perfect home for ‘Kill Jackie,’ said Jamie Lynn, EVP co-production & distribution EMEA. “As the platform continues to grow across Europe, we couldn’t be more delighted to embark on this adventure together. With its relentless pace, thrilling action and unforgettable central performance, we know ‘Kill Jackie’ is in the very best of hands. “ “I loved Nick’s gonzo thriller of a book,” Butterworth has said . “Our ambition is to twist and expand his world into something equally funny, dark, crazed and unique. Or die trying.” “Kill Jackie” is a “sly character study that asks what happens when you’re forced to act out your darkest impulses in order to survive. But at its heart, it’s a grounded, universal story about family: the kind we’re born with and the kind we choose,” Fremantle told Variety is the run-up to Mipcom. “Kill Jackie” is produced in partnership with José Luis Escolar’s Deabru Kalea Filmeak which supervised production in and around Bilbao. So expect the propulsive thriller to make full use of Bilbao’s extraordinarily chic post-industrial cityscape, taking advantage of its Guggenheim Museum, belle époque and modern plate glass architecture, estuary-adjunct walkways and green countryside. “Killing Jackie” is co-created by Conor Keane, Butterworth Peter Lawson (“John Wick”) and Thomas. Butterworth serves as both writer and showrunner. Executive producers are Lawson and Jose Agustín Valdés for Steel Springs Pictures, Butterworth, Thomas, Zeta-Jones, Rebecca Dundon, Dante Di Loreto and Jeffrey Levine, with Nick Harkaway serving as executive consultant. With the WBD deal, a multi-territory sales to Prime Video and a recent AMC+ U.S. sale, “Kill Jackie” has closed the lion’s share of major territories in the world. Zeta-Jones is represented by UTA and Ziffren Brittenham LLP. Butterworth is represented by Curtis Brown. Daniel Ings is represented by United Agents, WME, TFC Management, ColorCreative, Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern and CLD Communications. title: Black Lives Matter Commitments Failed To Bring About “Structural Change” In UK TV Industry, Finds Diamond Diversity Report
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Cristiano Ronaldo Reportedly Lining Up First Drama Series With Matthew Vaughn, Damian Lewis & Some Big Name Guest Stars Chris Brown Pleads Guilty To Affray Over UK Nightclub Confrontation View All July 28, 2026 1:00am The BBC & HBO's 'I May Destroy You': launched summer 2020 BBC/HBO Commitments made following the Black Lives Matter movement of summer 2020 failed to generate “embedded, structural change” in the UK TV industry, according to the latest Diamond diversity report. Paul Moore, chair of the Creative Diversity Network (CDN), which compiles the annual reports, said the recent decline in representation of Black, Asian and minority ethnic people both on and off screen shows progress has “stalled or drifted backward” since broadcasters made major promises more than five years ago. According to the report, the percentage of on-screen roles taken by Black, Asian and minority ethnic actors and presenters has plateaued since 2022 at 23.2%, while off-screen it has fallen by 1 percentage point to 13%. The latter figure is comfortably below the 17.9% national workforce average. Related Stories News Emmys On-Screen Diversity Hits 11-Year Low With 2026 Nominees News 'Police Academy' Reboot With Key & Peele Was Scrapped After Mike Brown Shooting, Says Writer: "We're Not Making A Cop Comedy Right Now" Sparked by the murder of George Floyd, the Black Lives Matter movement initially felt as though it was having a long-lasting impact across the pond. All broadcasters unveiled lofty commitments to improve diversity on and off-screen, while the topic dominated chatter at that year’s Edinburgh TV Festival amid critiques of sluggish diversity gains in an industry dominated by gatekeepers from privileged backgrounds. Watch on Deadline Diamond’s findings will therefore be a big disappointment to those at the coalface of improving representation for non-white people in the UK TV industry. They come a year after a weighty study found that Black professionals were experiencing systemic racism and faltering career progression, despite years of industry diversity initiatives. Of all the major networks based in the UK, Paramount, which owns Channel 5 (now 5), had the lowest proportion of contributions from Black, Asian and minority ethnic people, with the BBC top for on-screen and Channel 4 off-screen. The proportion of non-white people in senior roles has also fallen since 2022 to 12% and remains stubbornly at 2019 levels, the report found. Last year, this group took up only 10.9% of executive producer roles, for example. There were some green shoots, such as lead actors from non-white backgrounds hitting 34.9% last year, almost double the national workforce average, while writers from non-white backgrounds was up at 21.3%. But ultimately, Moore said Diamond’s tracking of UK TV industry diversity data over the past nine years shows flatlining progress. “The real power of Diamond lies in its ability to look beyond headlines and track changes over time to expose where progress has stalled or drifted backward,” said Moore, who is communications and corporate affairs chief at ITV. “For example, the recent decline in Black representation suggests that initial commitments made following the Black Lives Matter movement did not lead to embedded, structural change.” Earlier this year, the CDN revealed it was revamping Diamond , allowing for improved reporting, which will come into force later this year. title: Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa’s MultiChoice
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Stars Emma Sidi & Jack Shep To Join Sky & NBCU For Edinburgh TV Festival Masterclass Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa’s MultiChoice Curiosity Entertainment Enlists Execs Laurie Seidman And John Maatta & Sets Storyteller Media’s Debut Page-To-Screen Slate View All July 28, 2026 12:29am Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada Sylvain Lefevre/Getty Images The $2B acquisition of Africa’s MultiChoice has helped Canal+ post higher half-year revenues and earnings . Unaudited total group revenues saw revenues grow 40% to €4.29 billion ($4.88 billion), though without MultiChoice the growth shrinks to just 1.4% year-on-year compared to 2025’s €3.07B. Similarly, adjusted EBIT (before exceptional items) was up 68% to €433M, from €257M, and had a 10.1% margin. Excluding MultiChoice, the number drops to 13% growth. The market update comes just hours after London-listed Canal+ pledged more than €980M to French and European cinema over five years in a fresh deal with French entertainment bodies. The news was heralded as of unprecedented length for the Paris-based pay-TV giant. Related Stories News Canal+ Pledges More Than $1 Billion For French & European Cinema Over Five Years News Thabo Rametsi Unveiled As Apartheid-Era Music Legend Hugh Masekela In First-Look Image For Bill Condon's 'The Road Home' Canal+ this morning revealed it had hit its target of €250M in synergies resulting from its takeover of African pay-TV giant MultiChoice last year . Watch on Deadline The company has sought to significantly reduce costs in Africa since the buyout, with streamer Showmax discontinued earlier this year in one move that shocked the local industry. The H1 figures reveal Showmax made a €52M loss in H1 of 2025 on revenues of €23M. “Following the acquisition of MultiChoice, our increased scale is starting to deliver the benefits we expected,” said Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada . “We have achieved half of our €250M synergies target and remain well on track for the year, and we confirm our full-year and medium-term guidance.” Studiocanal Canal+’s production arm, Studiocanal, had an “excellent six months on and off screen,” according to Saada, who pointed theatrical successes such as Guru in France and Pressure in the US, and the biggest film deal at Cannes 2026, for The Midnight Library, which sold to Paramount for $36M . The content production, distribution and other segment, which includes Studiocanal and streamer Dailymotion, posted revenues of €356M, up 9.9% YoY. This accounted for 7.8% of Canal+’s overall revenues, down from 9.3% last year. Adjusted EBIT was €28M, which was 3% lower than 2025. “With a slate including Paddington 4 , Zack Snyder’s remake of Escape From New York , our first major South African film production, The Road Home , and Danny Boyle’s Ink , Studiocanal’s momentum looks set to continue,” he added. Back at group level, Saada pointed a systematic review of costs in France last year 2025 was benefitting finances, along with “strong D2C subscriber acquisition and lower churn, plus an ongoing shift to streaming in Poland. In Africa, adjusted EBIT was up 9% excluding MultiChoice, driven by pay-TV growth among other factors. Canal+ said its “turnaround” of MultiChoice was underway and pointed to a long-term rights deal for the Premier Soccer League in South Africa, the 2027 men’s and 2029 women’s rugby world cups across sub-Saharan Africa and a production slate including The Road Home , Heist of Benin and a screen adaptation of bestselling novel Americanah Subscriber acquisition was up 40% in MultiChoice countries compared to H1 2025 in MultiChoice countries, with June the best month “in a decade.” Adjusted EBIT at MultiChoice was up 160% to €143M, from €55M a year ago. This was primarily put down to synergies of €120M, including the impact of Showmax’s discontinuation. title: Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 27, 2026 11:00pm 'Bruton' Courtesy of JIB LLC Famous, or infamous, people make for good subjects of movies, whether documentaries, essay films or fiction features. Just look at the lineup of this year’s Locarno Film Festival , whose 79th edition , running Aug. 5-15, features all sorts of screen stories about bold or recognizable names. From a German entertainment figure and an Italian film and series creator to a U.S. prisoner sentenced for an “unintended crime,” the program of the Swiss festival allows you to learn more about people who have been in the headlines. Plus, there is also a cinematic letter to a documentarian of modern Lebanese history and a fiction feature about infamous Nazi Heinrich Himmler’s massage therapist. Related Stories Movies 'Heated Rivalry' Producer Brendan Brady Backs Yukon-Set Rom-Com 'From Me to You' (Exclusive) TV Think You Can Beat Darts Superstar Luke Littler? Netflix Opens Entries for Live Sports Show If you are curious about diving deeper into the lives of the famous and the infamous at Locarno 2026 , THR has compiled some possible picks for you below. Sixteen Moments of My Life ( Seize Moments De Ma Vie ) by Albert Serra Section: Out of competition ‘Sixteen Moments From My Life’ The new movie from Spain’s Albert Serra ( Afternoons of Solitude ) focuses on German actress and singer Ingrid Caven. Yes, that is THE Ingrid Caven who is best known for her roles in films directed by her former husband Rainer Werner Fassbinder, including Love Is Colder Than Death , Why Does Herr R. Run Amok? and The American Soldier . You may also remember her from her role as Miss Vendegast in Luca Guadagnino’s Suspiria (2018). Since this is a Serra film, this is not your typical documentary, of course. Here is how the Locarno festival website teases Sixteen Moments of My Life : “Ingrid Caven sings about 16 moments from her life in a unique concert at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris.” And Locarno artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro tells THR : “It’s a live concert that Albert worked on with Ingrid,” adding: “It’s one of the out-of- competition section films that could be very, very interesting” for audiences. Bruton by Vincent Grashaw Section: Out of competition ‘Bruton,’ courtesy of JIB LLC Last year, Vincent Grashaw was in Locarno with the indigenous crime drama Keep Quiet , starring Lou Diamond Phillips and Elisha Pratt. This year, he returns with a very different story set in the world of crime, a biopic about Bryan Bruton, who was sentenced to a decade in a Florida prison for an “unintended crime.” Or, as the Locarno festival synopsis reads: “A tragic accident leads Bryan Bruton on a wild and unforgettable experience in the Florida prison system.” The film stars Theo Rossi. Bruton was charged in the early 2000s with a manslaughter conviction for a fatal hit-and-run in Jacksonville, Florida. The movie follows Bruton’s journey through the correctional system. After his release, he moved to California and turned to making the YouTube video series Bryan Bruton Crazy Prison Stories . It covers life in the Florida prison system, from how inmates obtain and conceal drugs, alcohol and weapons to cutting the window out of a jail cell. Marco Bellocchio: La porta della Realtà by Fabio Lovino Section: Out of competition ‘Marco Bellocchio: La porta della Realtà,’ courtesy of Fabio Lovino The director worked as set photographer for legendary Italian writer-director Marco Bellocchio ( Portobello , The Traitor , Kidnapped ) for more than 20 years – long enough to have something to tell the world. “After 20 years of working with Marco Bellocchio, I felt the need to share what I experienced with him and give voice to the emotions and lessons I received,” reads a synopsis of the film. “An exclusive portrait of the man and artist told through interviews and unseen images from the set.” Among the people featured in the film are Bellocchio’s family, long-term collaborators and such prominent actors as Pierfrancesco Favino and Fabrizio Gifuni, as well as such directors as Marco Tullio Giordana . I Is Another by Felix Randau Section: Piazza Grande ‘I Is Another’ Courtesy of Anke Neugebauer/Ostlicht Filmproduktion/Wega Filmproduktion Fall 1952. Journalist Hedda and her husband ambush Felix Kersten, the former massage therapist to Nazi SS leader Heinrich Himmler, on a train. “Kersten claims to have helped thousands of concentration camp prisoners to freedom during the Nazi era,” reads a synopsis. “But Hedda has doubts, and what started as an interview quickly leads to a psychological cat-and-mouse game.” Writer-director Randau’s fiction feature has a star-studded cast, including Claes Bang ( The Square , Bad Sisters ) as Kersten, Valerie Pachner ( Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore , The Stories , Four Minus Three ) as Hedda and Susanne Wuest ( Sound of Falling , Goodnight Mommy ) as Kersten’s wife. What awaits audiences? Randau puts it this way in a director’s note: “Every story has three sides. Yours. Mine. And the truth…” Revolutionaries Never Die by Mohanad Yaqubi Section: Filmmakers of the Present Competition ‘Revolutionaries Never Die’ Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Yaqubi’s goal was to celebrate the legacy of the late Lebanese filmmaker Jocelyne Saab by tracing 16 of her films documenting Arab revolutions and struggles between 1973 and 1983. The result is Revolutionaries Never Die , a cinematic letter to the female filmmaking pioneer in response to an invitation that Yaqubi received from the late Lebanese director and that suggested a collaboration just two months before her death. “Since his reply can never reach her, the film transforms into a lyrical expedition through the life, political commitments and artistic vision of a singular voice from the era of revolution,” the Locarno website highlights. And Yaqubi notes in a director’s statement: “Jocelyne Saab’s film archive from 1973 to 1983 brought forward several questions about the striking resonance between her historical depictions and our contemporary realities five decades later, when no answers can ever be given.” Transition by Peter Badel and Chris Wright Section: Out of competition ‘Transition,’ courtesy of Grischa Meyer This film has a very personal story behind it; actually, more than one. Documentarian Thomas Heise began a film about Berlin’s Schönhauser Allee, the road he lived on for decades. A few months later, Heise died unexpectedly. Heise’s long-time cinematographer Badel and editor and co-director Wright stepped up to complete the film, though. “With exclusive material from his archives, the film reveals lived history and a great thinker,” Locarno’s website promises. Heise ( Vaterland , Material ), born in East Berlin in 1955, when Germany was divided into the GDR and West Germany, was known for chronicling the reality of life in East Germany and, after German reunification, the societal and social changes in the country. title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’
full_text: Jul 27, 2026 10:35pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’ 5 hours ago Sean Astin Says ‘I Had to Sell My House’ During ‘Lord of the Rings’ Era Because $250,000 Payday Was So Low: ‘I Negotiated Such a Small Amount on the Trilogy’ 14 hours ago Ryan Gosling Pitched His Own ‘Ghost Rider’ Movie to Marvel as Studio Slows Down Output to Restore Quality: ‘When Quantity Is So Much, You Get Spread Thin’ 14 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection “ Spider-Man : Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland ‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounded Spider-Man tale” that is “thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.” Fandango correspondent Erik Davis shared a glowing review on X , writing that director Destin Daniel Cretton’s sequel “feels deeper, more thoughtful and more mature than the previous trilogy.” Related Stories 'Avatar Aang' Team Reveals More Spinoffs in the Works, Nearly Making Katara Pregnant and Why Fans Shouldn't Watch the 'Dark Web' Leak Guillermo del Toro Says There Is 'Absolutely No Goddamn AI' in 'Pan's Labyrinth' 3D Re-Release: 'We're Protecting a Lineage of Art' “That maturity extends beyond the story to the action, with Cretton crafting some of my favorite Spider-Man fight sequences of the Holland era,” he added. “Part detective story, part psychological thriller, part buddy comedy (the Spider-Man/Punisher banter is so much fun), it stretches in exciting new directions before becoming a genuine love letter to the fans. When you see it, you’ll get it.” Popular on Variety Critic Wendy Lee Szany wrote on X that she has “no notes” for “Brand New Day,” which delivered “top-tier action” and a few “tearjerker” moments. TV host and entertainment journalist Brandon Pope echoed the praise. He wrote in his X review , “‘ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘ may be the most Marvel Marvel movie I’ve ever marveled. Destin Daniel Cretton honors beloved Spider-Man media — especially Raimi — to create something soulful + thrilling. Hulk, Punisher deliver. Big reveal lives up. The best of the Tom Holland Spidey series.” Film critic Peter Howell likewise adored the Marvel sequel. He wrote on X that “Brand New Day” cut back on the “multiverse tedium to give us a grounded Spider-Man tale that’s back to the city roots of the comic book hero we knew and loved.” “Tom Holland finally nails the sarcasm, angst and love hassles of Spidey/Peter Parker as Stan Lee first envisioned the character,” Howell added. “The film negotiates the emotional landmines left by ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ five years ago while a seriously scary villain emerges in the person of a malevolent telepath. Solid support from Zendaya , Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Mark Ruffalo and ‘Stranger Things’ star Sadie Sink.” Nexus Point staffer Kevin Verma wrote on X , “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is exactly the refresher Marvel needed. Tom Holland has never been better and the Spidey-Punisher pairing is pure gold. Destin Daniel Cretton outdoes himself, but the script is the real superhero- thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.” Holland returns as Peter Parker/Spider-Man in “Brand New Day,” which is set four years after the events of “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” That movie ended with Doctor Strange casting a spell in which Peter is erased from everyone’s memory, so now the web-slinger is fighting crime in New York City without the support of MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon). A new threat emerges in the form of Sadie Sink’s mysterious villain at the same time as Peter’s spider powers begin evolving beyond his control. The supporting cast includes Mark Ruffalo as Hulk and Jon Bernthal as Punisher. Expectations for “Brand New Day” are sky high after 2021’s “No Way Home” became a pop culture sensation with $1.9 billion at the worldwide box office. It was Holland’s second billion-dollar-grossing “Spider-Man” movie after 2019’s “Far From Home” earned $1.1 billion on the heels of “Avengers: Endgame.” While Marvel has had its ups (“Deadpool and Wolverine”) and downs (“Captain America: Brave New World”) in recent years, “Brand New Day” should get the MCU back on strong box office footing ahead of December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.” Holland played a greater role in the development of “Brand New Day” compared to his previous “Spider-Man” movies. He took deep dives on the internet to understand what exactly Spider-Man fans wanted to see in his latest outing as Marvel’s iconic web-slinger, then took these fan ideas directly to studio executives and the movie’s screenwriters. “What’s been really fun about this most recent movie is designing the suit and being a part of that process and understanding what we wanted to try and achieve,” Holland told LADbible about having greater involvement in the movie’s development this time around. “I have been actively sifting through the internet and trying to best understand what it is that the fans want from a ‘Spider-Man’ movie, and that’s been my driving force in these pitch meetings,” he added. “I think the producers, at times were like, absolutely sick of me, but I think it’s really important, because we make these movies for [the fans].” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opens in theaters nationwide July 31. But he's also painfully human so bring tissues 😭 Also the Tom/Zendaya chemistry was rom-com levels. And we need more Punisher in everything. And Sadie Sink… just wow! Liza too! pic.twitter.com/68jgm3htfs — Lyra Hale 🇵🇷🏳️‍🌈✍🏼 (@MsLyraHale) July 28, 2026 #SpiderManBrandNewDay is a triumph from Destin Daniel-Cretton. Bursting with heart, sincerity, hope. A story about the need to be vulnerable and human, to not let the world turn you into a monster, to recognize your pain in an effort to help others feel less alone in theirs. title: Tom Holland Says He’ll Play Spider-Man “For as Long as They’ll Have Me” After ‘Brand New Day’: “If This Movie Does Good, I Guess We’ll See!”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 10:06pm Tom Holland attends the Los Angeles premiere of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" at Dolby Theatre on July 27. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Logo text Tom Holland is swinging into his fourth Spider-Man film — and don’t expect it to be his last. At the Los Angeles premiere for Spider-Man: Brand New Day on Monday, the star reflected on his long journey with the character, telling The Hollywood Reporter , “There’s a family here at Marvel and Sony. We’ve been making these movies for 10 years and we’re all really good friends and we all still really love working with together and there’s a shorthand, there’s a collaboration, there is a shared love for this character that is Peter Parker. When we all get together, it always feels like something magical happens, and to get to do it time and time again is something that will never really sink in for me. It still feels like this is my first-ever premiere for this character. It has been the gift of my life.” Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day': First Reactions From the Premiere Movies Matt Damon Drops by Criterion Closet, Reveals Lesson Learned From Frequent Collaborator Steven Soderbergh: "You Want to Keep Pushing" The new movie is set four years after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home , where Peter Parker has been anonymously protecting New York City until his superpowers undergo a surprising and potentially dangerous evolution. First reactions to the film hit social media soon after the premiere ended. Asked about his future as the superhero, Holland responded with a smile, “I will do it for as long as they’ll have me. So if this movie does good, I guess we’ll see!” That’s probably a pretty safe bet, as Brand New Day is expected to be one of the biggest movies of the year at the box office — on the heels of fellow smash The Odyssey , also starring he and Zendaya. Tom Holland says he’d return for another #SpiderMan film at the #SpidermanBrandNewDay premiere. pic.twitter.com/vHcxmaRO94 — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) July 28, 2026 Holland has spoken about how he called Sony Pictures head Tom Rothman and persuaded him to push back the production of Spider-Man so that he could first film The Odyssey , with the filming dates originally conflicting. At the premiere, Rothman explained why he was willing to do so, saying, “We sort of recognized that it was a rare opportunity for him. It’s unusual, to say the least, that the two movies came out so close together but I’ve always believed that a rising tide lifts all boats. People are going to the movies again and The Odyssey is a great movie and people enjoy it. I think that’s ultimately going to be very good for Spider-Man as well.” The schedule meant Holland arrived to the superhero set with many lessons from Christopher Nolan fresh on his mind; director Destin Daniel Cretton recalled that as soon as they kicked off filming, his “work ethic was incredible, the passion for the craft, the ability to make daring choices. I think when he stepped onto our set, he was just like pumped and ready to go, and he wanted to make something really great. It was wonderful — I’ll take any actor coming off of a Christopher Nolan set because they’re like ready to work their butts off to get the best product possible.” Spider-Man: Brand New Day hits theaters on Friday. Tiffany Taylor contributed to this report. THR

Sony and Marvel’s Spider-Man : Brand New Day held its glitzy, star-packed world premiere at the Dolby Theater in Hollywood on Monday night, and not long after the screening ended, the first reactions began to flood social media. Destin Daniel Cretton ‘s Brand New Day is the fourth standalone Spider-Man film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — as well as the 38th film overall in the MCU — and picks up the action after 2021’s near $2 billion-grossing Spider-Man: No Way Home. The films once again are led by Tom Holland as Peter Parker/Spider-Man, as well as Zendaya as Michelle “MJ” Jones-Watson and Jacob Batalon as Peter’s best friend Ned Leeds. Related Stories Movies Tom Holland Says Some of His Movies Are "Sh**," Making Them Hard to Promote Movies The Doom Boom: Marvel Studios Brings 'Doomsday' and More to Its Most Crowded Comic-Con Panel Ever The MCU’s Jon Bernthal’s Frank Castle/Punisher, Michael Mando’s Mac Gargan/Scorpion and Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner/Hulk also appear in the film. New cast members include Severance ‘s Tramell Tillman and Stranger Things star Sadie Sink , the latter of whom is playing an unknown character which has led to feverish speculation online. “Keeping what Sadie’s doing under wraps, you’ll honestly understand when you see the movie. The movie is a better movie if you don’t know certain things,” Cretton said in a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter . The plot of Brand New Day follows the end of No Way Home , with the world — including MJ and Ned — having forgotten who Peter Parker is. Four years on, Peter is still protecting New York City as Spider-Man and he links up with street vigilante the Punisher to take on the likes of the Scorpion, all while his own powers undergo a new evolution. Brand New Day is written by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, who both co-wrote the other Holland Spider-Man films, including Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017), Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021). The film is produced Kevin Feige, Amy Pascal, Avi Arad and Rachel O’Connor. The film is part of Phase Six of the MCU and is followed by December’s Avengers: Doomsday in the Marvel continuity. title: Michael B. Jordan Reacts to David Jonsson’s ‘Black Panther 3’ Casting
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 9:54pm Michael B. Jordan at the 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Los Angeles premiere. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Logo text Michael B. Jordan is finally giving his thoughts on David Jonsson being cast as the new Black Panther in Ryan Coogler ‘s upcoming third installment in the superhero franchise. At Comic-Con 2026 over the weekend, Marvel revealed that Jonsson will star as an adult version of the son of T’Challa, portrayed by the late Chadwick Boseman in the 2018 original. Black Panther 3 will also film on 70mm and hit theaters Dec. 15, 2028. A few days after the announcement, Entertainment Tonight caught Jordan at the Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiere in Los Angeles Monday night to ask him about his thoughts on the casting. Related Stories Movies Eva Mendes Reacts to Husband Ryan Gosling's 'Ghost Rider' Casting Movies Marvel, 'Lanterns' and Johnny Depp: Here's What Hit (and Missed) at Comic-Con 2026 “Oh, I love it. It’s amazing! I can’t wait, can’t wait!” the Oscar winner said in an excited tone. View this post on Instagram Jordan — a longtime Coogler collaborator who won his first Oscar earlier this year for his role in the filmmaker’s Sinners — played villain Erik Killmonger in the 2018 film and the 2022 sequel, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever . It hasn’t been officially announced whether Jordan will reprise his role in the third film. After Boseman died in 2020 at age 43 following a battle with colon cancer, Jordan took to social media to pay tribute to his former co-star and friend. “One of the last times we spoke, you said we were forever linked, and now the truth of that means more to me than ever,” he wrote, adding, “I wish we had more time.” Earlier this year, when Jorden was honored at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival with the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award, he also took a moment to remember Boseman , saying that the late actor was with him throughout filming Sinners . “I loved that guy so much,” he added, “and it saddens me every time I think about it that I won’t get a chance to work with him again.” THR
