title: Netflix Sets Launch Date for Lee Chang-dong’s Awards Hopeful ‘Possible Love’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 27, 2026 8:44pm 'Possible Love' Netflix In a welcome piece of news for fans of Asian arthouse cinema, Netflix has set Lee Chang-dong ‘s much-anticipated drama Possible Love — the revered Korean auteur’s first film since 2018’s Burning — for a limited release in U.S. theaters on Oct. 23 ahead of its worldwide streaming launch on Nov. 6. Netflix is positioning the film — one of its most highbrow features of the fall — for an awards-season run. Possible Love will make its world premiere in September at the Venice Film Festival , where it will vie for the Golden Lion, followed by a North American debut as a gala selection at the Toronto International Film Festival. Related Stories TV Panta Mosleh's Queer Interfaith Comedy 'Pass the Salt' Adds to Cast (Exclusive) Movies Whoopi Goldberg, Jenifer Lewis, Vanessa Williams, Vivica A. Fox to Star in 'Women Like Us for Netflix Possible Love reunites Lee with two of his most accomplished earlier collaborators. The film stars Jeon Do-yeon, who won the Cannes best actress prize as the shattered lead of Lee’s Secret Sunshine in 2007, and Sul Kyung-gu, the unforgettable lead of the director’s early masterpieces Peppermint Candy (1999) and Oasis (2002). They are joined by Zo In-sung ( Moving , Escape from Mogadishu ) and Cho Yeo-jeong (best known globally as the gullible rich wife of Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite ). Netflix also shared a poster and a first-look still from the film on Tuesday along with the release plans. The poster shows the film’s two female leads, Jeon and Cho, standing apart beneath moonlit trees at dawn — the frame’s pervasive stillness carrying an unmistakable charge of unease. Similarly, the still shows the ensemble cast standing by the sea, with their glances carrying a complicated sense of emotional intrigue. Beyond the cast and art, little has been revealed about Lee’s new feature beyond an official plot summary: “ Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) — a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence.” Although he’s never received an Oscar nom or had a film make much international commercial impact, Lee’s work has accrued a level of reverence among global cineastes that few auteurs can match. Across six features in three decades, the novelist-turned-director — who also served, improbably, as South Korea’s culture minister in the early 2000s — has picked apart the emotional fault lines of Korean society with a spare, literary intensity. Along the way, he picked up Venice’s special director’s prize for Oasis , the Cannes screenplay award for Poetry (2010) and, with Burning , the Cannes critics’ prize and the distinction of becoming the first Korean film shortlisted for an Oscar in the international feature category. Lee co-wrote Possible Love with his Burning writing partner Oh Jung-mi. Pinehouse Film, the Korean outfit that also backed Burning , produces alongside Anonymous Content and NOWFILM. The film is a U.S.-Korea co-production. “I’m not the type of filmmaker who can make movies easily,” Lee said in a statement accompanying the release date announcement on Netflix’s Tudum site. “Before I begin a film, I must be certain of what it means — to me, to the audience, and to cinema itself. That is why Possible Love took so long to make.” Netflix THR

title: Co-Founders Of Magic Hour Entertainment And Rebelle Media Plus Author Duo Christina Lauren Advise Studios & Streamers To Devote Resources To “Elevated” And “Prestige” Romance Through Casting, Chemistry & More
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi David Jonsson To Play T’Challa’s Grown Son In ‘Black Panther 3’; Pic Hits Theaters In December 2028 – Comic-Con ‘Dark Matter’ Season 2 Trailer Debuts In Hall H At Comic-Con, Teasing Endless Possibilities With The Box ‘Spaceballs: The New One’ Invades Comic-Con With Send-Up Of Marvel’s Hall H Panels Of Yore View All July 27, 2026 5:10pm L-R: Rebelle Media's Laura Lewis and Amanda Palley & Max Siemers of Magic Hour Entertainment Rebelle Media/Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Paramount+ As Divergent author Veronica Roth pointed out in her opening of the “Romance: On the Big Screen: Why It’s About Damn Time” panel Friday at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, romance accounts for 23% of all book sales. So, while it may seem like the genre is having a moment on the big and small screens, it’s really always been a mainstay, and the entertainment industry is just loading up on what women audiences have wanted for a long time. Roth moderated the panel, which included Christina Lauren author duo Christina Hobbs and Lauren Billings, The Love Hypothesis and Love, Theoretically author Ali Hazelwood , One and Only author Maurene Goo plus Magic Hour Entertainment co-founder Max Siemers and Rebelle Media co-founders Laura Lewis and Amanda Palley . Related Stories Books Rebelle Media & MGM Television Win Rights To Adapt ‘When In Rome’ Series By Sarah Adams News Colleen Hoover Producing Ali Hazelwood’s Bestseller ‘Love, Theoretically’ At Amazon MGM Studios; Sofia Alvarez Directing “Romance onscreen has, and when I say onscreen, I’m talking about the theatrical screen, has dropped over 75% the last 20 years,” Rebelle Media ’s Laura Lewis said. “That audience hasn’t disappeared, and because of all the things that inspired us to get into the business — those Richard Curtis, Nancy Meyers and Nora Ephron movies and TV shows — we want to bring them back. So that’s what’s inspiring us to get on these books. Watch on Deadline Lewis’ partner Palley broke the news at the end of the panel that Rebelle Media has added Sarah Adams’ When in Rome series to their slate of book adaptations in development . The panel discussion revolved around the draw of romance, both in book form and tv and film form — whether adapted from novels or based on original screenplays — with insights from both authors and executives about how to get past the generic formula of putting a romance together. Most of the panelists favored leaning into specificity and the details that lovers of the genre latch onto while consuming a book, show or rom-com film. “It’s a really cool genre to be a part of because it is written primarily by women, not exclusively [and] primarily for, but not exclusively for women,” Billings said of romance. “It is a genre that embraces diversity. It embraces queerness, embraces so many things, and it has so much cultural and socio-economic power.” Billings and Hobbs, who have their book In a Holidaze coming to Netflix as a film adapted by Tiffany Paulson later this year, met 17 years ago sleeping on the sidewalk at the San Diego Convention Center waiting in line for the The Twilight Saga: New Moon panel featuring the cast of the then upcoming film. Reflecting on this anniversary, Billings commented on the growth of romance publishing’s presence at the convention. Max Siemers, co-founder of the newly-formed Magic Hour Entertainment, which is now behind an adaptation of Christina Lauren’s Love & Other Words , broached the idea that certain times of year (likely Christmas and Valentine’s Day) provide windows to release romantic comedies and dramas set specifically around those holidays but with only really that as the framework.

title: D4vd Ordered To Stand Trial For Murdering, Dismembering 14-Year-Old Girl
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Denise Petski , Dominic Patten July 27, 2026 4:20pm D4vd looks on from behind his defense attorney Marilyn Bednarski during his arraignment Monday Getty UPDATED: A Los Angeles judge has ordered singer D4vd (real name David Anthony Burke) to stand trial on murder charges in the killing and dismemberment of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has been charged with one count each of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains. The criminal complaint also includes special circumstance allegations of murder of a witness, murder for financial gain and murder by means of lying in wait as well as a special allegation that Burke personally used a deadly and dangerous weapon, a sharp instrument, to commit the crime. “The people have met their burden on all counts,” Judge Charlaine Olmedo said. She ordered that Burke continue to be held without bail. He has pleaded not guilty. Watch on Deadline If convicted, Burke could face the death penalty or life in prison without parole. A decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made at a later date. “What was presented by our Office over the course of the last week is a small but illustrative fraction of the evidence investigators have accumulated that proves defendant Burke is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt of the brutal murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez,” Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said. “This has been a parent’s worst nightmare, hearing the ghoulish details of how their child was killed, dismembered and left as trash.” Burke is to be arraigned on August 31. PREVIOUS, April 20, 2026: Seeking a quick trial, D4vd entered a not guilty plea Monday in a brief appearance in a downtown Los Angeles criminal court. Facing first-degree murder and continuous sexual abuse charges with the death penalty over the dismembered killing last year of teen Celeste Rivas Hernandez, the 21-year-old singer (whose real name is David Anthony Burke) sat behind a glass barrier this afternoon in L.A. Superior Court Judge Theresa McGonigle’s courtroom. Related Stories Legal D4vd Faces Possible Death Penalty Over Murder Of Teen & “Unlawful Sexual Acts” Charges News Singer D4vd Arrested In Connection With Celeste Hernandez’s Murder After Dismembered Body Found In Tesla “We believe the actual evidence will show David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez,” defense lawyer Blair Berk told the judge and attendees after entering pleas for her client. “We would like to have the evidence come into the light of day, at the earliest opportunity,” Berk added, requesting a fast-tracked preliminary evidentiary hearing. Berk made a point of wanting everything open in court, noting “there have been four months of secret grand jury proceedings.” In response, Deputy DA Beth Silverman said that her boss Nathan Hochman and the prosecution’s office would be “very happy to put on the evidence we’ve collected against Burke. A formal felony complaint ( read it here ) against D4vd was filed at the same time in LASC. Before the judge, Berk lamented the lack of discovery the defense has received so far, and at the same time, as Silverman objected that the evidence collected so far was “voluminous” noted the DA’s office had the time for a detailed press conference on the case earlier Monday. As Silverman cast doubt on there being much material available for a planned follow up hearing later this week, Berk asked the prosecution to endeavor with “conscientious earnestness” to get as much discovery as possible to her team. Amidst all that, Hernandez’s parents were seated nearby in the the Clara Shortridge Foltz Criminal Justice Center during the arraignment proceedings. The booking photo of D4vd aka David Anthony Burke, revealed before the start of a press briefing Monday Getty Earlier in the day at a press conference on the case, LA County DA Hochman said the “Romantic Homicide” singer could be executed if found guilty by a jury due to “special circumstances” that permit the rare use of the death penalty in California. Part of that special circumstance, according to the DA, is for D4vd “lying in wait, murder for financial gain and killing a witness in a criminal investigation” last April. That witness was the then-13-year-old Hernandez, who was allegedly the victim of sex crimes perpetrated by the TikTok sensation. Hernandez was last seen April 23, just before she went over to D4vd’s L.A. home. D4vd is also facing charges of “lewd and lascivious sexual acts” with an individual under 14 years of age. Similar to the alleged murder of Rob and Michelle Reiner last year by their youngest son Nick, the DA has not made public whether prosecutors will seek the death penalty or go for life without parole for D4vd. After months of investigation, D4vd was arrested last week at his rented Hollywood Hills residence . The arrest came almost eight months after Hernandez’s decomposed and mutilated body was discovered in the trunk of an impounded Tesla registered in the singer’s name. At that time, D4vd was on tour and out of L.A. Through representatives, he promised to cooperate with the LAPD and other law enforcement on the matter. Now behind bars without bail, D4vd is scheduled to be back in court Thursday. Also in court today, Judge McGonigle (who is overseeing the Reiner case as of right now) ordered the L.A. County medical examiner’s office to release the autopsy report for Hernandez. The report is not available because “the Department of Medical Examiner has not yet received notice the court order sealing the case has been lifted,” the department told Deadline. That paperwork is expected to arrive in one form or another at the medical examiner’s office by Tuesday morning, I’m told. Denise Petski contributed to this report .
